Inline comments start at an unquoted ' #' or ' ;'. Values may be wrapped in double quotes,
which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).
A repeated key in the same section overrides the earlier value.
Keys before any section go into section "".
"""


def _strip_inline_comment(value):
    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()


def parse(text):
    out, sec = {"": {}}, ""
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line[0] in "#;":
            continue
        if line.startswith("["):
            sec = line[1:-1]
            out.setdefault(sec, {})
            continue
        k, _, v = line.partition("=")
        key = k.strip().lower()
        value = _strip_inline_comment(v)
        out[sec][key] = value

Inline comments start at an unquoted ' #' or ' ;'. Values may be wrapped in double quotes,
which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).

Keys before any section go into section "".

    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()


def parse(text):
    out, sec = {"": {}}, ""
    for line in text.splitlines():

            sec = line[1:-1]
            out.setdefault(sec, {})
            continue
        k, _, v = line.partition("=")
        key = k.strip().lower()
        value = _strip_inline_comment(v)
        out[sec][key] = value

    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

        else:

Inline comments start at an unquoted ' #' or ' ;'. Values may be wrapped in double quotes,
which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).
A repeated key in the same section overrides the earlier value.
Keys before any section go into section "".
"""


def _strip_inline_comment(value):
    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()

            out.setdefault(sec, {})

k, _, v = line.partition("=")
key = k.strip().lower()
value = _strip_inline_comment(v)
# A value may be wrapped in double quotes; strip that wrapping.
if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == '"' and value[-1] == '"':
    value = value[1:-1]

which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).
A repeated key in the same section overrides the earlier value.
Keys before any section go into section "".

def _strip_inline_comment(value):
    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()

displayContent.text:
"""Tiny INI-like parser.

[section] headers; `key = value` lines; blank lines and lines starting with # or ; ignored.
Inline comments start at an unquoted ' #' or ' ;'. Values may be wrapped in double quotes,
which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).
A repeated key in the same section overrides the earlier value.
Keys before any section go into section "".
"""


def _strip_inline_comment(value):
    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()


def parse(text):
    out, sec = {"": {}}, ""
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line[0] in "#;":
            continue
        if line.startswith("["):
            sec = line[1:-1]
            out.setdefault(sec, {})
            continue
        k, _, v = line.partition("=")
        key = k.strip().lower()
        value = _strip_inline_comment(v)
        # A value may be wrapped in double quotes; strip that wrapping.
        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == '"' and value[-1] == '"':
            value = value[1:-1]
        out[sec][key] = value

"""Tiny INI-like parser.

[section] headers; `key = value` lines; blank lines and lines starting with # or ; ignored.
Inline comments start at an unquoted ' #' or ' ;'. Values may be wrapped in double quotes,
which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).
A repeated key in the same section overrides the earlier value.
Keys before any section go into section "".
"""


def _strip_inline_comment(value):
    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()


def parse(text):
    out, sec = {"": {}}, ""
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line[0] in "#;":
            continue
        if line.startswith("["):
            sec = line[1:-1]
            out.setdefault(sec, {})
            continue
    k, _, v = line.partition("=")
    key = k.strip().lower()
    value = _strip_inline_comment(v)
    # A value may be wrapped in double quotes; strip that wrapping.
    if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == '"' and value[-1] == '"':
        value = value[1:-1]
    out[sec][key] = value
    return out

"""Tiny INI-like parser.

[section] headers; `key = value` lines; blank lines and lines starting with # or ; ignored.
Inline comments start at an unquoted ' #' or ' ;'. Values may be wrapped in double quotes,
which are removed and protect # ; = inside. Keys are case-insensitive (lowercased).
A repeated key in the same section overrides the earlier value.
Keys before any section go into section "".
"""


def _strip_inline_comment(value):
    """Drop the inline comment portion of a raw value.

    A comment begins at an unquoted '#' or ';' that is preceded by
    whitespace. While a run of double quotes is open, those characters are
    literal and no comment is recognized.
    """
    result, i, n = [], 0, len(value)
    in_quotes = False
    while i < n:
        ch = value[i]
        if in_quotes and ch == '"':
            # close the quoting run; keep it for the next strip
            in_quotes = False
            result.append(ch)
        elif in_quotes:
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch == '"':
            # enter quoted region
            in_quotes = True
            result.append(ch)
        elif ch in "#;" and (i == 0 or value[i - 1].isspace()):
            # unquoted comment marker following whitespace -> cut
            break
        else:
            result.append(ch)
        i += 1
    return "".join(result).strip()


def parse(text):
    out, sec = {"": {}}, ""
    for line in text.splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line[0] in "#;":
            continue
        if line.startswith("["):
            sec = line[1:-1]
            out.setdefault(sec, {})
            continue
    k, _, v = line.partition("=")
    key = k.strip().lower()
    value = _strip_inline_comment(v)
    # A value may be wrapped in double quotes; strip that wrapping.
    if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == '"' and value[-1] == '"':
        value = value[1:-1]
    out[sec][key] = value
    return out
